supports: charsRequired is an int and is incremented once per character of the input string with no upper bound check
after the loop it is incremented once more for the terminator
malloc_fcn is called with charsRequired * sizeof(XML_Char); on 64-bit, sizeof(XML_Char) is 1 in the default build, so the product wraps when charsRequired wraps
memcpy then copies charsRequired * sizeof(XML_Char) bytes using the same wrapped value, producing an over-read or heap overflow depending on the wrap
copyString is called from parserInit (line 1090) and XML_SetEncoding (line 1241) with the user-supplied encoding name
the fixed function declares charsRequired as size_t
the same loop and the same multiplication are used, but size_t cannot wrap for any buffer that the process can actually address
the only change in the commit is the type of charsRequired
the diff changes int charsRequired = 0 to size_t charsRequired = 0
the commit message states copyString is only used for the encoding string supplied by the library user
the commit changes only expat/lib/xmlparse.c

The trigger requires an encoding name of gigabyte scale supplied by the embedding application, which the advisory notes is often a hardcoded constant; the practical attack surface depends on the application, not on document content.
The advisory says a 64-bit machine is needed; the arithmetic analysis was done for the default XML_Char=char build and not for every configuration.
The OSV fixed event names the 2.4.5 release-preparation merge commit (97a48405), not the code fix efcb3474; release tag ancestry and source were used to confirm the fix.
The MITRE CNA record is a placeholder (n/a vendor/product/version, no metrics or problemTypes); CVSS 7.5 and CWE-190 come from NVD.

critical_operation.description: copyString counts the input with an int and multiplies that count by sizeof(XML_Char) for both malloc and memcpy. If the caller-supplied encoding name is longer than INT_MAX characters, the counter wraps; the allocation then uses a wrapped (small or negative-derived) size while memcpy still copies the same wrapped byte count, yielding denial of service. The 2.4.5 fix widens the counter to size_t.

entry_point.description: parserInit calls copyString for the encodingName passed to XML_ParserCreate (line 1090), and XML_SetEncoding calls it again at line 1241. The vulnerable input is the encoding name supplied by the library user at parser creation or via XML_SetEncoding, not document content.
